description: Keeps OpenTelemetry Collector version pins in sync across TheWeatherCompany repos. A repo opts in by adding to its renovate.json: "extends": ["github>TheWeatherCompany/mwt-renovate-config:otel-collector"]. See README.md for which repos/files this is meant to cover and why.

customManagers.description: Any repo's Helm-chart-managed EKS otel-collector deployment - matches any path containing otel-collector/environments/<file>.tfvars, regardless of what precedes it (mwt-ee-deploy uses terraform/compute/services/..., mwt-ewb-deploy uses infra/...). Public upstream (open-telemetry Helm repo) - no gating needed.
otelcol-contrib image tag baked into the Helm values (same tfvars files as above, separate knob). Public upstream (Docker Hub) - no gating needed.

EC2-classic per-app agent config consumed by mwt-deploy's installOpenTelemetry.sh, e.g. mwt-config-api/scripts/otel-api.json, mwt-forecasteditor-api/otel-*.json, mwt-widgets/otel-web.json, etc. Gated: this datasource is TheWeatherCompany/mwt-observability's own GitHub releases, and mwt-observability's update-observability.yml only tags an otel-collector-vX release *after* sync-binaries has mirrored that version's RPM to S3. This prevents proposing a version that installOpenTelemetry.sh would 404 on at deploy time.

mwt-perforce-deploy: same RPM as above, pinned as a Terraform variable default instead of a JSON config (terraform/modules/perforce-server/variables.tf). Same gated datasource as the JSON manager above.

AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) collector image pinned by tag and digest as a Terraform variable default named otel_image, e.g. max-ondemand-skybase modules/pgdog/variables.tf and modules/pgcat/variables.tf (the pgdog and pgcat ECS metrics sidecars). Renovate replaces the tag and the digest together. Only matches a default that already carries a digest, so a tag-only default is left alone rather than tracked without one. Public upstream (ECR Public), no gating needed.

packageRules.description: Ordered broadest-first: Renovate merges packageRules in order, later rules override earlier ones on conflicting keys, so more specific tiers below must come after this one to win. Default: treat any file not matched below as prod-tier. Longer soak, and no automerge: the last two rules turn it on only where a merge cannot reach prod.

Staging-tier files: let dev soak for about a week first. Broad substring match (not prefix/suffix-anchored) since environment naming varies by repo: stg.tfvars, stg-blue.tfvars, stage.tfvars, staging.tfvars, etc. all qualify. Scope is already narrowed by each customManager's managerFilePatterns above, so a broad match here is safe.
Dev-tier files: propose immediately, no soak required. Broad substring match, same reasoning as the staging rule above.

One-time bootstrap: otel-collector-v0.156.0 was backfilled as a GitHub release on 2026-07-14, for a version that had actually been mirrored to S3 weeks earlier (before the gate-release step existed). Without this, the prod-tier 14-day minimumReleaseAge above would count from the backfilled release's creation time, not the real mirror date, delaying the very first catch-up bump for no reason. Matches on matchCurrentValue (the fleet's current pins, 0.150.1 and the stale 0.132.0), not matchNewValue - Renovate evaluates minimumReleaseAge per-candidate-release before the target value is renamed to newValue, so matchNewValue never actually matches at that stage. Remove this rule once every repo has moved off these two values - future releases go through the normal tiered soak above.

ADOT image: ECR Public gives Renovate's docker datasource no release timestamps, and under the default minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour (timestamp-required) the tiered soak above would hold every ADOT bump as pending forever. Seen with renovate 44.164.9 in a local lookup run on 2026-10-16: v0.50.0 was marked pending for exactly that reason. timestamp-optional lets these bumps through with no soak; automerge stays off, so a human still reviews each PR.

EC2 app configs (otel-*.json): automerge. These PRs target the repo's default branch (dev) after the prod-tier soak, and the new version reaches prod only with the app's next release. internalChecksAsSuccess because some of these repos run no CI on the PR, so Renovate's own stability check is the only one, and by default Renovate does not count it. Merges only on weekday working hours, when someone is around to notice.

mwt-ee-deploy dev and staging tfvars: automerge. A merge rolls nothing, since non-prod lanes deploy by workflow dispatch. Prod tfvars, mwt-ewb-deploy's gitops pins (Argo deploys from them) and mwt-perforce-deploy stay manual.
